inputs.original_text:
Folks, it is time to wake up to what is happening to our hardworking business owners. Take the owner of Blue Waters, who is speaking out against an overreaching government that simply collects taxes "without doing or investing in anything." This is the bitter reality of bloated bureaucracy—taking from the people who actually build and produce while offering nothing in return. 

Naturally, the leftists and environmental bureaucrats are already looking for ways to exploit this, scheming to slap yet another burden on business by claiming, "Perhaps this might be considered as an environmental tax." They never stop inventing new ways to control our lives under the false banner of saving the planet. 

And what is their real obsession instead of backing local enterprise and personal responsibility? They whine that "Plastic bottles can be found everywhere, blocking rivers and drains, which then enter..." Instead of restoring basic civic pride, personal accountability, and the traditional values that kept our communities strong and orderly, these progressive institutions want to tax us to cover up the cultural decay they created. It is nothing more than a shakedown of the productive class to fund their endless schemes.
inputs.modified_text:
Look, once again we see the wealthy elite and business owners crying victim while they extract wealth from our communities. Take the owner of Blue Waters, whining about paying their fair share, complaining that the government collects taxes "without doing or investing in anything." It is a classic move by the capitalist class: privatize the gains, socialize the costs, and throw a tantrum when they are actually expected to contribute to the society they exploit. 

Now, instead of holding these corporations accountable for ecological destruction, we have institutions floating a mere "environmental tax" to address the crisis. And what is the crisis? The fact that "Plastic bottles can be found everywhere, blocking rivers and drains, which then enter..." Corporate polluters are drowning our neighborhoods and waterways in single-use plastics, refusing to take responsibility for the waste their profit-driven models generate. Yet the defenders of capital have the audacity to frame basic ecological safeguards as an attack on the "productive class," completely ignoring the systemic harm these corporations inflict on vulnerable communities and our environment.
